
=================================================================
#57 Heaven–Earth King  (태초)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: The Fall of Euija · tone: island folklore
Logline: In the beginning there were two suns, two moons, and nobody ever got a decent night’s sleep.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ The first night, the king of Tamla pours two cups. His guest stays by the door, busy being wronged.
[1] ¶ Yuri Dora has a fire going and no plan to ask permission.
[2] Gyebek: The order was not his. / It had his seal. It was not his.
[3] Yuri Dora: That’s the third time tonight.
[4] Gyebek: The fourth.
[5] Yuri Dora: Ha. Then you want the one about a world stolen fair and square. / I’ll start at the beginning. / Sit or don’t.
[6] ¶ **Gyebek** stays standing by the door. Yuri Dora starts anyway.
[7] ── SCENE: Two Suns ──
[8] ¶ In the beginning there were two suns and two moons. By day people dropped in the fields with their hoes still in their hands; by night they froze in their own doorways. Nobody ever had a decent night’s sleep or a decent harvest, and the old died faster than anyone could bury them.
[9] ¶ Above all of it sat **Heaven–Earth King**, who ran the living and the dead out of one office and therefore never went home. One night he fell asleep at the desk anyway, and dreamed he was eating: one sun, one moon, swallowed whole, one of each.
[10] [CARD Heaven–Earth King: The god with two jobs and one desk. He dreams about breakfast.]
[11] Heaven–Earth King: ……Huh. / One each. / I ate one of each. / Ha— that’s a son. Someone’s going to shoot those down.
[12] ¶ He comes down to the world to find the mother of that dream, and finds her in the poorest house on the road: a girl the village calls **the Lady of Wisdom**, a hearth with no fire in it, and a rice jar she does not open in front of guests.
[13] Lady of Wisdom: Who are you.
[14] Heaven–Earth King: Someone passing. / A hungry one.
[15] Lady of Wisdom: ……Sit, then.
[16] ¶ She goes round the back and lifts the lid of the jar. The bottom of it looks up at her. She puts the lid back as if that might help, ties up her hair, and walks across the road.
[17] ¶ Across the road lives **Sumyung Jangja**, who is rich the way a flood is wet. He has nine storehouses, a horse that kicks beggars, a dog that bites whatever the horse misses, and a rice measure that comes out a little smaller when he lends and a little larger when he collects.
[18] Lady of Wisdom: Lend me one measure of rice. / I have a guest.
[19] [CARD Sumyung Jangja: The richest man under two suns. He lends one measure and collects two.]
[20] Sumyung Jangja: One measure. / Two when you pay it back. / A guest? Anyone who’d come to your house, I can guess.
[21] Lady of Wisdom: Two, then.
[22] ¶ He fills the measure himself, with his back to her.
[23] ¶ She washes it nine times at the well and spends the last of her firewood on it. The king takes the first spoonful. Something in his mouth grinds.
[24] Heaven–Earth King: …… / Your rice has a bit of bite to it.
[25] Lady of Wisdom: ……It’s sand. / I washed it nine times.
[26] Heaven–Earth King: Who gave it to you.
[27] Lady of Wisdom: The house across the road. / I said I’d pay back two.
[28] Heaven–Earth King: Two. / One measure with sand in it, for two. / ……Eat. Eat all of it. I’m stepping out for a minute.
[29] ¶ Sumyung Jangja is counting his storehouses, which is how he prays, when the sky over the ninth one goes black at noon. The horse will not kick. The dog gets under the porch.
[30] Sumyung Jangja: Who’s there. / There’s nobody under heaven who can touch me.
[31] Heaven–Earth King: That’s why I came from above.
[32] Sumyung Jangja: ……W-what is it you want. / Rice? If it’s rice— two measures, no, ten, the whole storehouse—
[33] Heaven–Earth King: Without the sand?
[34] ¶ The floor of the ninth storehouse opens. The richest man in the world goes down through it, past the dirt and past the dark, into the place under everything where the measures are honest. He is the first one there. He will not be lonely for long.
[35] ¶ He goes back across the road. He stays until the day the calendar allows, and the morning after, he is already tying his sleeves.
[36] Lady of Wisdom: You’re going?
[37] Heaven–Earth King: Lots of work upstairs. / There are two suns, remember.
[38] Heaven–Earth King: Two sons. The first one out is Big Star, the second one Little Star. / When they turn fifteen, have them plant these.
[39] ¶ Two gourd seeds in her palm, and half of a wooden comb. The other half goes into his sleeve.
[40] Lady of Wisdom: ……Fifteen years.
[41] Heaven–Earth King: …… / Thanks for the rice.
[42] ¶ She has twins. The elder comes out quiet and looks at everything. The younger comes out already complaining. They grow up under two suns and two moons, and get asked whose sons they are in every yard in the village.
[43] [CARD Big Star: Big Star, the elder twin. He would rather be right than first.]
[44] [CARD Little Star: Little Star, the younger twin. He would rather be first.]
[45] Little Star: Mom. Who’s our father. / The other kids are at it again.
[46] Big Star: Leave it. Mom’s tired.
[47] Lady of Wisdom: ……When you’re fifteen.
[48] ── SCENE: The Gourd Vine ──
[49] ¶ At fifteen she puts the seeds in their hands and the half comb in the elder’s. They plant them by the wall at dusk. By morning the vine has gone past the roof, past the clouds, and out of sight.
[50] Lady of Wisdom: Climb. / All the way up.
[51] Little Star: What about you?
[52] Lady of Wisdom: I’ll be here. I’ll have rice on.
[53] ¶ Little Star gets to the top first and pretends he wasn’t racing. The man at the top of the vine holds out his hand without getting up.
[54] Heaven–Earth King: The comb.
[55] ¶ Big Star puts the half in his palm. The king takes the other half out of his sleeve, where it has been for fifteen years, and fits them. The teeth close.
[56] Heaven–Earth King: ……Fits.
[57] Little Star: You never came down. Not once.
[58] Heaven–Earth King: ……There were two suns.
[59] ¶ He has a thousand geun of iron melted down into two bows and two arrows, heavy enough that nobody but a son of his could draw them, and walks the boys to the edge of the sky.
[60] Heaven–Earth King: Two suns, two moons. / Two of each over your mother’s roof for fifteen years. / One each.
[61] ¶ Big Star takes the sun at noon. He breathes out once and lets go, and the second sun breaks like a plate. Its pieces scatter east and stay there as stars. At midnight Little Star draws on the second moon and hits it square, and its pieces go west.
[62] Little Star: Brother. Got it in one. / You saw?
[63] Big Star: I saw.
[64] ¶ In the morning people go out to the fields and do not fall down. That night they sleep. Nobody thanks anyone, because nobody knows who to thank.
[65] Heaven–Earth King: Done. The world’s yours. / The living side and the dead side. You two decide who takes which. / I’m not deciding. Whoever I pick always comes back to argue. / I’m resting.
[66] ── SCENE: The Contest ──
[67] ¶ They decide it the way brothers decide things. Big Star proposes riddles, which suits the one who knows the answers.
[68] Big Star: Which trees keep their leaves all their lives, and which ones drop them?
[69] Little Star: Solid ones keep them. Hollow ones drop them.
[70] Big Star: Poor little brother, don’t talk about what you don’t know. / Bamboo and reeds are hollow at every joint, and they keep their leaves.
[71] Little Star: ……Another.
[72] Big Star: Why is the grass short on the hill and long down in the hollow?
[73] Little Star: Spring rain washes the hill’s dirt down into the hollow.
[74] Big Star: Then why is the hair on your head long and the hair on your feet short?
[75] Little Star: …… / That one’s cheating.
[76] ¶ Two for two. Their father, who said he would not decide anything, leans over the edge of his rest and drops two flower seeds between them.
[77] Heaven–Earth King: Flowers. / Whoever grows the better one gets the living side. / ……That’s me done interfering.
[78] ¶ They plant them in two silver basins and sit up with them. Big Star’s flower comes up green and keeps coming, and by the third evening it has opened. Little Star’s comes up yellow and leans.
[79] Little Star: Let’s sleep, Brother. / We’ll look in the morning. See whose did better.
[80] Big Star: All right.
[81] ¶ Big Star sleeps the way honest men sleep, all the way down. Little Star lies on his side and counts his brother’s breathing up to a hundred. Then he gets up, trades the basins, and lies down again in the same shape, so his brother will wake first.
[82] Little Star: ……Brother! Wake up! / Look, it’s mine!
[83] ¶ Big Star looks at the open flower in front of his brother, the one he watered for three days. He looks at the yellow one by his own hand.
[84] Big Star: …… / Yes. Your flower did well.
[85] ¶ He gets up and brushes the soil off his knees.
[86] Big Star: Brother, countless people live in the mortal world. Among them are thieves and swindlers. To govern them well you need strength and wisdom — but above all, a true heart. So govern them, and make a beautiful, peaceful world.
[87] ¶ He is already walking toward the dark edge when he says the rest, and he does not turn round.
[88] Big Star: But, little brother. You took it with a stolen flower. / The living world will have plenty of murder, plenty of treason, plenty of thieves, and plenty of people reaching for other people’s wives and husbands. / The law down below will run clear.
[89] Little Star: ……Brother! / Brother, that’s—
[90] ¶ **Big Star** goes down. **Little Star** keeps the warm side.
[91] ¶ It goes the way his brother said, and worse, because Little Star had never thought about the parts he didn’t want. The trees still talk. So do the birds, the cattle and the stones, mostly about him. When a mother calls her son’s name at dusk a ghost answers too, and the living and the dead walk the same roads in the same clothes, and nobody can tell which is which.
[92] Little Star: Brother. / Brother, help me, just this once. / The trees talk. The ghosts answer. I can’t tell who’s a man and who’s a ghost.
[93] ¶ Big Star comes up. He scatters five measures of pine-bark powder over the world, and the trees and the birds and the cattle go quiet and have stayed quiet since. Then he hangs a scale from the sky.
[94] Big Star: Line up. / A hundred geun or more, you stay up here. / Less, you come with me.
[95] Little Star: ……And the thieves? The ones who kill people?
[96] Big Star: Those are your flower.
[97] ¶ He goes back down with the light ones following him in a long quiet line. Since then the dead weigh less than the living, the law below runs clear, and the law up here belongs to Little Star. Under Big Star, **Yumla** judges, and the measures are honest.
[98] ── SCENE: The Fire ──
[99] ¶ The fire has gone low. Gyebek sat down at some point and does not remember when.
[100] Gyebek: ……Did the brother know. That the flowers were switched.
[101] Yuri Dora: He knew.
[102] Gyebek: And he gave it up anyway.
[103] Yuri Dora: He did. And he went down. / Down there is the dead world, up here the living. There’s a flower field out at the western end, and above all of it, old Lord Hwanin. / Three Realms, all told. Tonight you only need the two.
[104] Gyebek: ……Rice with sand in it.
[105] Yuri Dora: Hm?
[106] Gyebek: Nothing.
[107] ¶ It is the first story on the island he does not inspect.
[108] ¶ **The next night Gyebek finds a roof to mend. Yuri Dora finds a ladder. One woman made this island, and she was enormous…!**
